Published online: April 20, 2026 View All Announcements Thank You: 2024 JAMDA Scientific Reviewers Opens in new window [PDF] Call for papers Immunization Recommendations, Barriers and Facilitators in PA-LTC Environments Opens in new window Across the lifespan, immunizations are a powerful force in helping to protect people against potentially devastating diseases and maintaining health. Older adults in post-acute and long-term care environments are at particular risk for infections preventable by vaccination due to immunosenescence and living in communal settings. Moreover, they have more serious sequelae following these infections including cardiovascular events and functional decline. When immunized as recommended by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), risks of developing pneumococcal disease, shingles, influenza, and other vaccine-preventable conditions is reduced. Further, immunization of staff members helps to prevent the transfer of pathogens to these individuals. Despite recommendations the majority of older adults are not fully immunized. This special issue intends to disseminate immunization rates in PALTC and innovative approaches to overcome challenges and increase immunizations among older adults and their caregivers.
